To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the surface charge of phagosomes is controlled by the phosphoinositide composition of the membrane and by the presence of phosphatidic acid, that this charge controls the localization of polycationic proteins by electrostatic association, and that this mechanism of protein targeting can be turned on and off.
anionic phospholipoids control the fate of proteins by electrostatic interactions.

the membrane of nasient phagosomes becomes increasingly anionic during phagocytic cup formation and that this change in charge is instrumental in the recruitment of polycationic proteins to the phagosome.
In summary, our research is concerned with

elucidating the role played by electrostatic interactions in the regulation of signal transduction and, in particular, with the contribution made by anionic lipids and their associated proteins to the orchestration of the phagocytic process.
the mechanisms by which the cell senses and responds to the presence and distribution of anionic lipids.
the mechanisms that control the assembly and the function of membrane domains and how they contribute to the spatiotemporal regulation of signal transduction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study of cell signal transduction has benefited greatly from the development of digital imaging techniques, and that the future of this field promises even greater advances.
the electrostatic switch is not only on, but it is also on all the time.
the electrostatic switch is a powerful tool in the control of signal transduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
electrostatics play a key role in the control of protein targeting during phagocytic signal transduction.

the membrane of the nascent phagosome undergoes a highly choreographed series of changes in its phospholipid composition and surface charge, and that these changes are instrumental in recruiting and positioning a number of proteins that are required for phagocytotic signal transduction.
the lipid composition of a cell membrane is not only a determinant of the membrane's structure, function, and dynamics but also a key regulator of protein targeting and signal transduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phospholipids and their derivatives can be used as molecular tools to control the spatial and temporal distribution of signal-transducing proteins and, thus, regulate cell signaling.

the membrane is not a static platform, but rather a dynamic and highly plastic structure, capable of undergoing rapid, large-scale rearrangements that are controlled by changes in its lipid composition.
the lipid composition of membranes is a dynamic and regulated feature of cell signaling and that electrostatic interactions are important determinants of protein targeting.
